scope: the agent command path on a ShowRecordV2 behind the route gate: the v2 candidate-delivery admission, version dispatch through the executor, editor admission and both command catalogues, and the v2 route's agent binding
invariants: One writer: an agent candidate adopts through the same store session, revision, history, save queue, rollback and supersession the v2 route's typed UI intents use; the same intent through either path yields deep-equal records and equal history depth.

Distinct checks, in order: session and revision, Show presence, prepared-capture currency, candidate identity, provisional v2 schema, validateShowRecordV2 domain, Pattern/Library/control dependencies, zero write, compiler eligibility through the captured Stage - never one normalize-and-accept.
A refusal or no-op returns the original record identity and creates no history entry, provider save or ordering stamp.
The editor and its commands are one version for one Show: the route declares the version it holds, the executor dispatches on the captured record, and read_show answers in that version.

Folding applyShowCommandV2 onto the executor's result vocabulary loses nothing: changed, unchanged and refused map to changed, noop and refused with the v2 issues intact, and a refusal keeps the private candidate open.
Nothing widens: no compiler, schema or command-domain capability is added, and the v2 catalogue is #1041's landed vocabulary used unchanged.
SHOW_V2_ROUTE_DEFAULT stays false; every v2 surface here is reached only through the development opt-in.

candidate shape: valid, raw-schema-invalid, domain-invalid, an authoring-schema document delivered in place of a record, and byte-equal to the current record
dependencies: resolvable Pattern source, a newly introduced unavailable source, a pre-existing missing source under the capture baseline, and a Stage map the candidate moves to
admission currency: current capture, superseded record, replaced dependency set, unmounted route, provider swap
settlement: saved, superseded by a later adoption, and rolled back by a failed save
operation identity: first delivery, duplicate delivery of the same candidate, a changed candidate on the same operation, and a duplicate begin key
content: final-content deletion leaving a validated empty Show, and a Show that still compiles

Manual/command parity: the same Show End through admitShowV2PilotSetShowEnd and through set_show_end

residualGaps: SHOW_V2_ROUTE_DEFAULT is still false. Nothing here flips it, and every v2 surface remains behind the development opt-in.
The agent harness (agent:smoke, agent:corpus, agent:baseline:fixtures) still speaks v1 vocabulary. Its rewrite belongs to the flip, not to this slice, and the dispatch excludes a corpus rewrite.

Stable diagnostic resize retry has no v2 counterpart: the v2 catalogue has no qualified single-command resize recomputation, so a v2 editor answers not_qualified rather than approximating the intent. Recorded as an accepted narrowing of a v1-only diagnostic, not of authoring.

The v2 route binds no field-activity scope, so a v2 candidate never waits on active input. The wait machinery is wired and the admission honours a timing deadline; only the route's dirty-field registration is absent.

The declared affected set from runShowCommandV2Transaction is reported to the caller with each change and is not consumed by admission. No catalogue invariant makes it checkable: rename_show reports a real change with an entirely empty affected set, so refusing an empty declared set would refuse a valid command.

The MCP server resolves the bound record's version with one exempt account read per request. It is deliberately not a resolve, which would consume the pending binding-moved notice and spend a rate-limited agent call, but it is one extra Durable Object read per MCP request.

The browser declares its record version at registration. It selects discovery only; the executor still dispatches on the captured record, so a wrong claim narrows the offered tools rather than admitting a mismatched command.
The runtime MCP test supplies a minimal window surface because esbuild cannot bundle the Worker inside jsdom. The Chromium proof of the same route and binding is the authenticated e2e spec.
